headline: Failed Senate resolution would have required the President to remove U.S. troops from unauthorized hostilities with Iran.
what_it_does: This joint resolution would have directed the President to pull U.S. Armed Forces out of hostilities in or against Iran. That would apply unless Congress passed a declaration of war or a specific authorization to use military force against Iran. It would not have stopped the U.S. from defending itself, its personnel, or its facilities abroad from an attack. The Senate refused to take it up or end debate on it on March 24, 2026.

who_it_affects.how: The President would have been required to end U.S. military involvement in hostilities with Iran unless Congress approved it.
Troops taking part in hostilities in or against Iran would have been withdrawn from those operations, though they could still defend against attacks.
Congress would have had to pass a declaration of war or a use-of-force authorization before U.S. forces could continue hostilities with Iran.
